title: QuantHarness: Price-Driven Multi-Agent LLMs for High-Frequency Trading

task.value: Short-horizon (high-frequency) directional trading using a multi-agent LLM framework that operates solely on OHLC price data and technical signals.
task.quote: To bridge this gap, we introduce QuantHarness, the first multi-agent LLM framework explicitly designed for high-frequency algorithmic trading.

architecture.value: LangGraph system with IndicatorAgent, PatternAgent (multimodal chart pattern matching), TrendAgent (OLS trend channels), RiskAgent (fixed stop-loss, LLM risk-reward ratio), and DecisionAgent outputting LONG/SHORT over next three candles; zero-shot, no fine-tuning.
architecture.quote: The system decomposes trading into four specialized agent, IndicatorAgent, PatternAgent, TrendAgent, and RiskAgent, that communicate through structured prompts.

data.value: 1-hour and 4-hour OHLC bars from YFinance and TradingView for BTC/USD, CL, ES, NQ, QQQ, SPX, DJI, VIX (and DAX at 1h); 5,000 bars per asset, 100 sampled segments of 100 candles each.
data.quote: All historical price data used in the benchmark are obtained via the publicly available APIs, specifically YFinance and TradingView’s historical market data services. We use 1-hour and 4-hour OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) candlestick data for all assets to maintain consistency in time resolution.

window.value: 4-hour data spans e.g. DJI/QQQ/SPX 2015-08 to 2025-05, BTC 2023-04-01 to 2025-06-23; 1-hour data e.g. BTC 2025-02-21 to 2025-09-13. Segments randomly sampled; XGBoost trained on 50 files, tested on remaining 50.

baselines.value: Random selection, Linear Regression on 40-bar closing-price slope, XGBoost on TA-Lib indicators; TradingAgent also appears in Table 1.
baselines.quote: We evaluate four categories of baselines: (i) Random Methods, which performs random selection of market trend between LONG and SHORT and risk-reward ratio \in[1.2,1.8] . (ii) Linear Regression, which serves as a rule-based baseline.

headline_result.value: On 4-hour bars, NQ accuracy 55.3 (+26.5% over random baseline), R_cc 0.216; SPX accuracy 63.7 (+34.6%).

costs.value: Returns use simulated stop-loss of 0.05% and LLM-set take-profit; no transaction costs, slippage or inference costs stated.
costs.quote: We adopt a fixed stop-loss threshold \rho=0.0005 (i.e., 0.05%), selected to reflect the relatively small fluctuations typical within a short three-candlestick forecast horizon, consistent with prior work (Kissell, 2013).

leakage_controls.value: Last three candles of each 100-candle segment withheld during inference to prevent test-time leakage; no discussion of LLM training-data contamination.
leakage_controls.quote: From this, 100 evaluation segments per asset are sampled, each with 100 consecutive candlesticks—the last three withheld to prevent test-time leakage.

limitations.value: Accuracy degrades on ultra-short candles (~1–15 min) due to noise; architecture not truly real-time because LLM and tool calls add latency exceeding 1-minute opportunity windows.
limitations.quote: Second, the architecture is not truly real‑time. Each inference cycle involves an LLM call plus several bound indicator/pattern tools, introducing latencies that can exceed the window in which a 1‑minute opportunity remains exploitable.

release.value: Code on GitHub at Y-Research-SBU/QuantHarness, plus a project website.
